content:
macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6 introduces a redesigned set of traffic light window control buttons. The new design references earlier Mac OS X systems, with more detail on each button.

On the Mac, the three traffic light buttons are an iconic design for managing windows. The red, yellow, and green circles handle closing, minimising, and maximising windows respectively.

macOS 27 Golden Gate includes many small changes, among them recently redesigned app icons.

However, the traffic light button changes affect every app window, and also look a bit like the classic Aqua design from the early OS X era.

For me, whether it's iOS 27 or macOS 27, the best part of Liquid Glass is these moments that recapture the Aqua style.

Here is what the new traffic light window control button design actually looks like in action:

macOS 27 Golden Gate also fixes window shape consistency. macOS 26 Tahoe used things like wind speed or water temperature to decide the shape of app windows. Now it's just one metallic-style Dock option... or is it just me?

macOS 27 Golden Gate is currently available as a developer and public beta download, with the official release expected in September.

This update also refreshes the Preview app icon to the new design version that first appeared in iOS 27 beta 5 last week.
